install_tell: roscore (interactive) OR roslaunch <pkg> <file>.launch OR docker run -p 11311:11311 osrf/ros:noetic-desktop-full roscore
misconfig_patterns: ROS1 master has NO authentication concept. caller_id parameter is identification, not authentication. Any client that reaches port 11311 can call any XML-RPC method.
Default bind 0.0.0.0 — internet exposure is purely a routing/firewall question, no in-product control.
getSystemState returns the complete topology graph (publishers, subscribers, services) in one call — full robot stack census from one read.
getParam / getParamNames frequently leak credentials, cloud API tokens, model paths, calibration secrets stored on the parameter server.
registerPublisher + publish to /cmd_vel (or equivalent motor topic) lets an unauth caller physically move the robot — the Brown 2018 paper demonstrated this with consent.
ROS1 Noetic EOL May 2025; no further security patches upstream. Install base lingers in academia + legacy industrial.
docker-compose patterns in published tutorials hardcode `11311:11311` port exposure — leaked verbatim in many GitHub repos.
Co-deployment with rosbridge_server (9090) + web_video_server (8080) on the same /32 is the headline exposure class.

active_probe.false_positive_check: rosmaster getUri returns a three-element XML-RPC array: [status_code int, status_message string, master_uri string starting with 'http://']. Reject if response is XML-RPC fault for unknown method (then it's generic XML-RPC, not rosmaster). Reject if body contains 'WordPress' or 'xmlrpc.php' (WordPress XML-RPC). Reject if Supervisor 'system.listMethods' signature returns (Supervisor's XML-RPC RPC interface). Confirm with secondary getSystemState call returning array of three arrays (publishers, subscribers, services).

shodan_dorks.notes: Insight #93: basic dork is port-free so it catches rosmaster relocated to non-11311 (11315/11316/11317 alt-ports for parallel ROS networks). Strict + version are port-pinned and high-precision but blind to relocated masters. XML-RPC fault body is shared with WordPress xmlrpc.php and Supervisor — disambiguate via active getUri probe. Shodan-dark concern HIGH: port 11311 is non-standard and Shodan banner-grab on it is inconsistent. Censys cross-population delta expected at Stage 0b. The Brown 2018 paper (DeMarinis et al., arxiv:1808.03322) is the historical population baseline: 100+ rosmasters per scan, 28 countries, 70%+ on .edu/research networks.

deployment_tells: TurtleBot 2/3/4 — roscore on the onboard NUC or Raspberry Pi, ROS1 Kinetic/Melodic/Noetic.
Clearpath Husky / Jackal — Ubuntu 18.04 + ROS1 Melodic factory image.
PR2 legacy Willow Garage installs still in long-running university labs.
Docker image osrf/ros:noetic-desktop-full is the canonical container; docker-compose with `ports: 11311:11311` is the standard leak.
Systemd unit wrapping `roslaunch <pkg> <file>.launch` for production robots.
ROS_MASTER_URI env var on every ROS node points back to host:11311 — leaks self-identity.
Cert subject-CN patterns: typically NONE (most ROS deployments are plain HTTP/XML-RPC, no TLS). When TLS present, robot.<lab>.<univ>.edu is the common pattern.
Edge boards: NVIDIA Jetson (Nano/Xavier/Orin) and Intel NUC dominate the host CPU.
pivot_paths: POST / getUri → master self-identity (URI) — fingerprint anchor
POST / getSystemState → complete [publishers, subscribers, services] graph — gold standard enum
POST / getPublishedTopics → topic + msg type registry
POST / getParam → parameter values (credential / token / path leak hotspot — read selectively)
POST / lookupNode → node XML-RPC URI (per-node API endpoint discovery)
POST / lookupService → service URI (per-service endpoint discovery)
vulnerabilities: CVE-2020-10289 — ros_comm DoS via crafted message types (Alias Robotics).
Alias Robotics RVD (Robot Vulnerability Database) catalogs ~200 ROS-ecosystem issues, most without CVEs.
No CISA KEV entries for ROS as of 2026-06-09.
do_not_call: POST / registerPublisher — injects rogue publisher (preludes a publish to robot command topic; this is the move-the-robot primitive)
POST / unregisterPublisher — deregisters a legitimate publisher
POST / registerService — injects rogue service handler
POST / unregisterService — tears down legitimate service
data_class: robot topology + parameter-server contents (frequent credential/token/path leakage) + indirect physical-motion capability when chained with registerPublisher+publish. NOT user PII directly, but exposes operational robot state and the means to control physical actuators.
restraint_notes: Topology read = POST / getSystemState + POST / getPublishedTopics + POST / getTopicTypes (three read-only calls cover the full graph).

Parameter read = POST / getParamNames first; read selected getParam values only when names suggest secret-leak (e.g. /robot/api_key, /credentials/*, /aws/*). Stop at name enumeration when sensitive — names ARE the finding.
NEVER call register*/unregister*/setParam/deleteParam — these mutate the master state and the registerPublisher path leads to robot motion.
Insight #93: pair port:11311-pinned dork with at least one port-free anchor to catch relocated masters.
Insight #12 shadow-sweep: every confirmed rosmaster gets a 9090 + 8080 + 11345 cross-port check on the same /32.

version_history_auth_relevant.ROS1 Box Turtle (2010-03): first ROS1 release; no auth, no auth on roadmap
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS1 Melodic (2018-05): no auth change; Brown paper scan period (Dec 2017 — Jan 2018) caught this generation
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS1 Noetic (2020-05): final ROS1 release; no auth added; EOL May 2025
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS2 transition: ROS2 abandons the central master entirely (DDS discovery); SROS2 layers cert-based auth on top of DDS — but the install base of ROS1 lingers
